correctness.rationale: For each integer \(n\ge3\), the majority update on the sunlet has an exact two-step identity equivalent to two local pair-symbol constraints. The 16-state transfer trace counts all labelled period-dividing-two states. An exact characteristic polynomial in the package gives the stated Lucas/residue evaluation, and two 4-state subtransfers prove fixed and pure counts. An elementary strict-decrease energy rules out longer periods. The independent C++ direct dynamics check exhaustively counts states for \(3\le n\le11\); a separate integer-matrix certificate verifies all three characteristic polynomials and trace sequences for \(3\le n\le30\). The proof, not finite extrapolation, establishes the quantified all-n result. The \(O(\varphi^n)\) error and exponential ratios follow from Lucas roots.

value.rationale: The sunlet is a canonical connected unicyclic graph with the smallest one-leaf memory decoration of each cycle site. The theorem gives complete natural periodic invariants for every n, rather than a routine cutoff: F_n, P_n, pure two-cycle counts, all primitive two-cycles, and sharp asymptotic proportions. The exponential proliferation from <=1 two-cycle on the undecorated cycle to asymptotically \(\varphi^{2n}/2\) on its sunlet and exponentially rare all-vertex toggling reveal a structural effect of pendant memory not implied by generic two-period theory. This supplies reusable exact benchmarks for nonlinear threshold dynamics.
